plain_english: Under the Conservative Joint Policy (Disparity detected if either Alg 1 or Alg 2 rejects H0), the global federated model demonstrates statistically fair performance. Neither test found significant evidence to reject the null hypothesis of equal performance at alpha = 0.05. Alg 1 p-value: 0.3883, Alg 2 p-value: 0.4010.

alg1_result.null_hypothesis: H0: mu_1 = mu_2 = ... = mu_K = mu (Equal client performance)
alg1_result.alternative_hypothesis: H1: mu_i != mu_j for some i != j (Performance disparity exists)
alg1_result.interpretation: The test statistic T1 = 25.3239 does not exceed the critical value at alpha = 0.05 (p = 0.3883 >= 0.05). We fail to reject the null hypothesis. Cross-client performance differences are consistent with random estimation variation.

alg2_result.null_hypothesis: H0: mu_1 = mu_2 = ... = mu_K = mu (Equal client performance)
alg2_result.alternative_hypothesis: H1: mu_i != mu_j for some i != j (Performance disparity exists)
alg2_result.interpretation: The Welch-type test statistic F = 1.0462 with df = (24, 1796.5) is not significant (p = 0.4010 >= 0.05). We fail to reject H0. Model performance is statistically homogeneous across clients under heteroscedastic conditions.
